content.stringValue:
Chapter 1 showed different kinds of work. Social status means a person's position in society. It is more than a job: it can affect recognized rights, duties and freedom. The same task does not mean two people have the same choices.

Use a specific example rather than one pyramid for every island. Juan de Plasencia, a Spanish missionary writing in 1589, described Tagalog communities using terms including maharlika and different forms of alipin. His account is one outside view, written after Spanish arrival, not the voice of every community.

In that account, maharlika were free people with duties to a datu. Aliping namamahay could live in their own homes and have property while owing service. Aliping sa gigilid served within another household, with greater restrictions; the account says people in this category could be sold. These were unequal conditions, not simply voluntary jobs.

Other sources use terms such as timawa, and social arrangements varied. Do not automatically match every Tagalog label with a Visayan label. Compare the place, source, duties and freedoms before deciding whether two groups were alike.

content.stringValue:
The clever-bird tale in this scene is made up for this app. It is not an authentic story from a named Philippine community. It illustrates how listening and retelling can work; it is not evidence that a real community told this tale long ago.

In the fictional scene, a storyteller describes a clever bird finding a path through a storm. Children listen, ask about unfamiliar words and try retelling the story. They should identify it honestly as a classroom story rather than give it a false ancient origin.

An oral tradition is knowledge or expression passed through speaking, singing, chanting and listening across generations. A documented example is the Hudhud narrative chants of the Ifugao. These are not the same as our invented bird tale.

Worked example for a careful learner: Step 1. Ask who is sharing the account and where it comes from. Step 2. Ask what it means and how it may be shared. Step 3. Credit the source when discussing it. Studying a tradition does not require performing a ceremony or sharing your own religious beliefs.

content.stringValue:
Religious teaching and political leadership are related histories, but not the same event. The Sheikh Karimul Makhdum mosque site in Simunul is associated in official commemoration with 1380. This is a milestone linked with Islamic teaching and community worship, not a date when everyone in the islands adopted Islam. It also does not mean every part of the present building was built in that year.

In the 1400s, the Sultanate of Sulu developed under leadership associated with Sharif Abu Bakr, also known as Shariful Hashim. Sources give differing exact dates in the middle of that century, so this teaching timeline uses the broader period. A sultanate is a political system led by a sultan.

Compare what the two labels describe: one concerns a remembered religious milestone; the other concerns political organization. Muslim communities and sultanates did not all develop at the same time. Local leaders continued to matter, and the Sulu sultanate did not govern the whole Philippine archipelago. You do not need to memorize an exact founding year to explain this distinction.
